Subject: Optimize toolkit pricing + tech fit for payments reconciliation

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the intro. We evaluated Redwood's hosted API for a small POC and now are looking at the Optimize toolkit (batching/caching/quantization guidance + tooling) as part of a production push for our payments reconciliation pipeline. Two quick things we need to understand before we talk dollars:

- Technical: for our workload (~120M tokens/month, 99th pct latency target ~300ms), what quantization profiles and batching/kv-cache TTL do you recommend to meet SLO while preserving reconciliation accuracy (~>98% match rate)? Any accuracy caveats we should expect when switching to q8 or q4 variants?
- Commercial: how is the Optimize toolkit priced (credits vs seat vs committed bundle)? Any pilot/discount path for a 12-month commit?

Attaching a short summary of our performance targets. Would love a simple commercial option set + what rollback/fallback looks like if quality regressions occur.

Best,
Sara
Sara Holloway
Head of ML Platform, Lumen Financial
[sara.holloway@lumenfin.com]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: Sun, 13 Dec 2026 11:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Optimize toolkit pricing + tech fit for payments reconciliation

Sara — thanks for the clear ask and the targets. High-level response (summary + attached pricing grid):

Commercial options (summary):
1) Pay-as-you-go Optimize Add-on: no commit, billed per optimized token + seat for ops console. Good for short pilots.
   - Reference: $0.0025 per optimized token (estimate; depends on model/quantization).
2) Committed Credits + Optimize Bundle (recommended for your scale): 12-month commit, discounted credits + toolkit seat + 24/7 support.
   - Example: 120M tokens/month -> annual commit = 1.44B tokens. Suggested band: $X per token after 18% volume discount (see attached grid). Includes 10% onboarding credit.
3) Enterprise Dedicated Offer: reserved capacity + toolkit + SLOs (for stricter latency/throughput guarantees).

Technical recommendations (for 120M tokens/month, 300ms 99p):
- Quantization: start with q8_0 (8-bit symmetric) for the 13B family we benchmarked — best cost/quality tradeoff. If you need additional cost reduction, we can test q4_0 on a per-prompt eval; expect ~8–12% accuracy drop on worst-case prompts (we'll validate on your eval set).
- Batching: continuous batching with dynamic batch target 8–16 depending on observed arrival rate. For reconciliation workloads with many short prompts, aim for batching target ~12 and a max latency window of 25–40ms to meet 99p 300ms.
- KV caching: prefix/KV caching for repeated account/context tokens — TTL 30–60 minutes depending on data freshness. This typically reduces token spend by ~15–35% on reconciliation jobs.
- Fallbacks: automatic fallback to a higher-precision model (or hosted route) on detected quality regressions. We recommend a canary rollout with A/B evals for 2 weeks.

Pilot suggestion: 6-week pilot using q8_0 + batching target 12 + 30-day cache TTL. We'll run pre/post evals on your reconciliation test set and commit a credit rebate (up to 25%) if the rollout causes measurable regressions.

Attaching: optimize-pricing-grid-v3.pdf (pricing bands + example math), SOW draft placeholder for pilot.

If that looks reasonable, can you confirm monthly token expectations and whether Lumen prefers a single invoice or split by product line? Happy to set a follow-up call Wednesday.

—Karthik
Senior Solutions, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Karthik — thanks for the thorough write-up. A few points from procurement:

- We can commit to 12 months but need better visibility on unit economics. For a 12-month commit at our scale (120M tokens/mo), we are targeting a 25% total cost reduction vs our current self-managed baseline. The 18% discount you mention gets us part of the way there, but not to our target.
- Can you remove/reduce the one-time onboarding fee?
- We need an explicit SLO for inference latency on the committed offer (99p < 300ms) and a service credit if missed.

Also: two technical asks — can you quantify expected token reduction from caching for our exact pattern? We can share a 48-hour trace if useful.

If you can get closer to 22–25% discount with a waived onboarding fee and the SLO commitment, we can execute quickly.

Thanks,
Mike Chen
Director, Procurement, Lumen Financial
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Mike Chen <mike.chen@lumenfin.com>, Sara Holloway <sara.holloway@lumenfin.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Optimize toolkit pricing + tech fit for payments reconciliation

Mike / Sara — looping in Marissa (Sales Lead) and Laura (Pricing) to confirm final concessions. TL;DR: we can move on price with approvals but need the following structure: 

Counter proposal (commercial):
- 12-month commit at 1.44B tokens annual -> price: equivalent to an 18% discount off list for the Optimize bundle.
- Waive onboarding fee if Lumen signs an SLA addendum with a 12-month committed spend and standard usage reporting.
- Offer an additional one-time 6% credit (applied in month 2) if pilot meets accuracy targets in our A/B evals. Net effective first-year discount ~24% if pilot passes.

Operational/SLOs:
- 99p latency target < 300ms for the dedicated route or committed capacity; if we miss this SLA on a monthly basis, we offer a service credit (1% of monthly invoice per missed month, capped at 10%).
- We will run a 6-week pilot using q8_0, batching target 12, and a 30-min cache TTL. Redwood will provide a pre/post evaluation report on your reconciliation set.

Technical notes / caveats:
- q8_0 is our recommended default. q4_0 will reduce costs further but requires a per-prompt accuracy evaluation — not a general drop-in for reconciliation without validation.
- Caching benefit is workload-dependent; share a 48-hour trace and the infra team (cc'ed offline) will run a trace replay to estimate token savings. Typical savings we've seen for reconciliation workflows: 18–32% depending on repetition patterns.

Next steps:
1) Laura to post final SOW and pricing grid in Drive (attached SOW draft today).
2) Sara to approve pilot timeline (we propose Jan 4 start).
3) Lumen to confirm legal review cadence — we can send DocuSign once SOW is finalized.

Marissa / Laura — can you confirm approval for the one-time 6% pilot credit and the SLA service credit structure?

Thanks,
Karthik
(On behalf of Sales)
